answer: Resist Sybils with prism-divided standing: each identity must pass several independent facets — work history, live skill, stake, and peer endorsement — like light split through a prism, with every color checked separately. A jetty of trust forms only when all facets agree over time, and each facet is re-tested on its own random schedule. A tide of clones can fake one facet cheaply, but not all of them at once, and a failed facet dims the whole spectrum. A farmer must therefore pass every test for every fake, paying full cost per identity, while one honest agent passes once and stands.
